questions.question: What is the core production invariant for model serving?
options: Admit only work the fleet can finish inside an explicit service contract.
Keep every request in a queue until compute becomes available.
Maximize average accelerator utilization regardless of deadlines.
Use the same serving framework for every model and workload.
questions.explanation: A bounded service protects deadlines, memory, tenant budgets, and downstream capacity by rejecting or redirecting impossible work early.

questions.question: Why can a larger batching window reduce useful goodput for an interactive workload?
options: It always lowers device throughput.
It spends the latency budget before execution, so more completed requests may miss their deadline.
It disables request validation.
It forces every model to use stateful execution.
questions.explanation: Batching may improve execution efficiency while adding queue delay. Useful goodput counts only work completed inside the product contract.

questions.question: A pool receives 180 requests/s. Each warm replica sustains 30 requests/s at the chosen utilization target. You require one replica of failure headroom. What is the minimum warm target?
options: 5 replicas
6 replicas
7 replicas
31 replicas
questions.explanation: Steady demand needs 180 / 30 = 6 replicas. Adding one replica of failure headroom produces a target of 7.

questions.question: When is a prediction cache unsafe to reuse?
options: When the exact input, model, policy, tenant scope, and parameters all match.
When the response is small.
When a model, policy, authorization boundary, or stochastic decoding parameter changed but the key did not.
When the artifact digest is immutable.
questions.explanation: Prediction reuse is a correctness and isolation decision. Every input that can change output or authorization belongs in the key or must disable reuse.

questions.question: Why is queue age often a better autoscaling signal than GPU utilization for a tight online SLO?
options: Queue age can expose deadline pressure before all waiting work reaches the accelerator.
GPU utilization cannot be measured.
Queue age guarantees new replicas start instantly.
Queue age removes the need for a warm capacity floor.
questions.explanation: Utilization is commonly a lagging signal. Queue age observes waiting work earlier, though the scaling plan must still include provisioning and model-load delay.

questions.question: A model process is alive but its requested weights are still loading. Which health state should prevent normal traffic?
options: Liveness only
Readiness
Task-quality evaluation only
No health state; the gateway should retry every request
questions.explanation: The process may be live while it is not ready for the requested model and version. Readiness should remain false until usable serving capacity exists.

questions.question: What is the main trade-off in locality-aware routing for a multi-model fleet?
options: Warm model hits can reduce cold loads, but concentrating requests can create queue imbalance.
It removes the need for model versioning.
It guarantees every cache entry is authorized.
It makes autoscaling instantaneous.
questions.explanation: A robust route score combines model residency with queue pressure and deadlines instead of optimizing only warmth or only balance.

questions.question: During a zone loss, what is the safest retry behavior for timed-out inference?
options: Retry without a limit while original work continues.
Send duplicate requests to every surviving worker.
Propagate cancellation, use a bounded retry budget, and reject or use an explicit compatible fallback when capacity is exhausted.
Disable admission control until the zone returns.
questions.explanation: Bounded retries and cancellation prevent retry amplification. Fallback must preserve a declared product and quality contract.
